title: Cross-species insights from ART-D to uncover evolutionarily conserved oncogenic mechanisms.
authors: Guo, Yifan; Zheng, Jiadong; Wu, Yixin; Zhao, Kun; Lv, Dian; Liu, Wenhan; Wang, Mengling; Lu, Jin-Yu; Xu, Wenyan; Wang, Xianping; Ma, Xianjue
one_liner_zh: 该文构建果蝇Ras驱动肿瘤图谱，聚焦肿瘤演化信号通路，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，仅用机器学习做多组学整合，与本课题无关。
abstract: Cancer arises from oncogenic clones, yet the dynamic mechanisms driving their stepwise evolution toward malignancy remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish the Atlas of Ras-driven Tumors in Drosophila (ART-D), a systematic, cross-species platform that dissects the molecular and phenotypic trajectories of tumorigenesis across ten genetically defined Ras(V12)-driven models. By integrating longitudinal phenotypic profiling, we define three conserved stages of tumor development-initiation, promotion, and progression-distinguished by distinct shifts in tumor burden and tumor-induced cachexia. Transcriptomic analysis reveals stage-specific signaling rewiring: early tumorigenesis is characterized by co-activation of JAK/STAT, NF-kappaB/Toll, and MAPK pathways, whereas malignant progression is driven by Notch hyperactivation and Hippo pathway inactivation. Through integrative multi-omics and machine learning, we uncover an evolutionarily conserved pathogenic network coordinating JNK, NF-kappaB/Toll, Notch, and Hippo signaling, which we functionally validate across species. ART-D serves as a transformative resource bridging Drosophila genetics and human cancer biology, offering a robust framework for decoding conserved oncogenic principles and identifying of stage-specific vulnerabilities in RAS-driven cancers.
abstract_zh: 癌症源于致癌克隆，然而驱动其向恶性肿瘤逐步演进的动态机制仍未完全阐明。在此，我们建立了果蝇Ras驱动肿瘤图谱（Atlas of Ras-driven Tumors in Drosophila, ART-D），这是一个系统性的跨物种平台，用于解析十个基因定义的Ras(V12)驱动模型中肿瘤发生的分子和表型轨迹。通过整合纵向表型分析，我们定义了肿瘤发展的三个保守阶段——起始、促进和进展——这些阶段以肿瘤负荷和肿瘤诱导恶病质的显著变化为特征。转录组分析揭示了阶段特异性的信号重连：早期肿瘤发生以JAK/STAT、NF-kappaB/Toll和MAPK通路的共激活为特征，而恶性进展则由Notch过度激活和Hippo通路失活驱动。通过整合多组学和机器学习，我们揭示了一个进化上保守的致病网络，协调JNK、NF-kappaB/Toll、Notch和Hippo信号传导，并在跨物种中进行了功能验证。ART-D作为连接果蝇遗传学与人类癌症生物学的变革性资源，为解码保守的致癌原理和识别RAS驱动癌症中的阶段特异性脆弱性提供了稳健框架。
